description_en: The inscription is on a large boulder situated on the side of a path 400 meters east of the village of Kālikā Bajār (Kālikoṭ).The inscription is facing north-west. It is composed of two lines, together measuring 220 x 70 cm.The first line, inscribed in Rañjana script, contains the mantra of Avalokiteśvara. The line below it is written in Nāgarī script and contains the name of the king under which the inscription was carved. This king is Pṛthvīmalla, a famous Khaśa Malla king who ruled over west Nepal from circa 1338 to 1358 (Adhikary 1988;Andolfatto 2019).The document is typical of inscriptions from the 1350's, whereOṃ maṇi padme hūṃ, Avalokiteśvara's mantra, is written in Rañjana, followed by a text in Nāgarī. Similar inscriptions are found on the Patharnauli reservoir in Dullu (DLK0160) and on the Kuchi Bihāra stūpa and reservoir (ACH0010).The inscription was first mentioned by Yogi Naraharinath (Naraharinath VS 2013 (1956), p. 75) and by Giuseppe Tucci (Tucci 1956, p. 43).
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)

historical_events.event_description: The text of the inscription is as follows:1.oṃ maṇi padme hūṃ’2.maṃgalaṃ bhavatu śrī pṛthvīmalladevaḥ | likhitamidaṃ puṇyaṃ jagatisiṃdasyā
